stories.title: The Suez Canal, opened to navigation in 1869
stories.summary: Egypt's sea-level canal links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea across the Isthmus of Suez. The Suez Canal Authority dates its opening to international navigation to 17 November 1869.

stories.script: The Suez Canal is an artificial sea-level waterway across the Isthmus of Suez in Egypt. The Suez Canal Authority says it was opened to navigation on 17 November 1869. The pin is approximate.

cards.title: Suez Canal
cards.body: The Suez Canal Authority describes the canal as an artificial sea-level waterway running north to south across the Isthmus of Suez in Egypt, connecting the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea. Its official history dates the inauguration ceremony to 17 November 1869. The same official history records later turning points, including nationalization and a closure after the 1967 war, with reopening in June 1975.
cards.why: A primary official chokepoint on the globe, cited from the canal's own authority.

stories.title: The Antarctic Treaty, signed in 1959
stories.summary: The Antarctic Treaty Secretariat says the treaty was signed in Washington on 1 December 1959 by twelve countries active in the International Geophysical Year, entered into force in 1961, and now has 58 parties. Antarctica is reserved for peaceful purposes and scientific cooperation.

stories.script: The Antarctic Treaty Secretariat says the treaty was signed in Washington on 1 December 1959 and entered into force in 1961. It reserves Antarctica for peaceful purposes and scientific cooperation. The pin is a South Pole stand-in. A depositary report hosted by the Secretariat dates entry into force to 23 June 1961.

cards.title: Antarctic Treaty
cards.body: The official Antarctic Treaty Secretariat page says the treaty was signed in Washington on 1 December 1959 by the twelve countries whose scientists had been active in and around Antarctica during the International Geophysical Year of 1957-58. It entered into force in 1961 and, as stated on that page, now has 58 parties. Important provisions quoted there include that Antarctica shall be used for peaceful purposes only, and that freedom of scientific investigation and the exchange of scientific results shall continue. A depositary government report to ATCM 46, hosted by the Antarctic Treaty Secretariat, states that the treaty entered into force on 23 June 1961.
cards.why: The legal frame for a whole continent, cited from the treaty secretariat.

stories.title: The European Parliament's official seat in Strasbourg
stories.summary: Official European Parliament pages say EU governments decided in 1992 that the Parliament's official seat, and the venue for most plenary sessions, is Strasbourg, with additional work in Brussels and the Secretariat in Luxembourg.

cards.title: European Parliament seat
cards.body: An official European Parliament FAQ says the EU's national governments unanimously decided in 1992 to lay down in the EU treaty the official seats of the institutions. The official seat of the Parliament, and the venue for most plenary sessions, became Strasbourg; parliamentary committees meet in Brussels; and the Secretariat is officially based in Luxembourg. The same page says this arrangement was incorporated into the EU treaty in 1997, and that changing it would require treaty change. Official pages also say Parliament meets in plenary 12 times per year in Strasbourg for a four-day part-session, with additional part-sessions in Brussels. An official European Parliament document says the governments of the member states adopted the Edinburgh Decision on the location of the seats of the institutions on 12 December 1992, citing OJ 1992 C 341, p. 1. The Official Journal text itself was not fetched for this card.
cards.why: The official seat of the directly elected EU legislature, cited from Parliament's own pages.

stories.title: NOAA's Mauna Loa Baseline Observatory
stories.summary: NOAA's Global Monitoring Laboratory describes the Mauna Loa Observatory as an atmospheric research facility on the north flank of Mauna Loa, Hawai'i, continuously monitoring atmospheric change since the 1950s. Official coordinates and elevation are published on the observatory page.

The same page says the 2022 Mauna Loa eruption cut off road access, and that a temporary access road was completed on 26 March 2026, with no general-public opening date yet established.

stories.script: NOAA's Global Monitoring Laboratory places the Mauna Loa Observatory on the north flank of Mauna Loa, at 3,397 metres, and says it has been continuously monitoring atmospheric change since the 1950s. Official NOAA pages say the observatory was constructed in 1956 and has run continuously since, and that Keeling CO2 measurements began in March 1958. Official NOAA pages distinguish the 1956 construction from the March 1958 Keeling record. The pin uses the observatory's published coordinates.

captions.text: NOAA has monitored the atmosphere here since the 1950s.

cards.title: Mauna Loa Observatory
cards.body: The official NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory page says Mauna Loa Observatory sits on the north flank of Mauna Loa Volcano on the Island of Hawai'i, at an elevation of 3,397 metres (11,135 feet), and has been continuously monitoring and collecting data related to atmospheric change since the 1950s. It publishes the site coordinates as 19.5362° North, 155.5763° West. The page also states that the 2022 eruption of Mauna Loa cut off road access, that construction on a temporary access road was completed on 26 March 2026, and that no public opening date had yet been established when the page was read. NOAA's Global Monitoring Laboratory says the observatory was constructed in 1956 and has been continuously in operation since. A NOAA media release says Keeling CO2 measurements began in March 1958. These two official start statements are not collapsed into one day. The exact calendar day in March 1958 is [UNKNOWN] in this card.
cards.why: One of the world's primary climate-observing sites, with coordinates published by NOAA.

It says the District's first assignment was to reverse the flow of the river and protect the region's water resources, and that the MWRD reversed the Chicago River in 1900 by constructing the Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal to take wastewater away from Lake Michigan, discharging it to the Des Plaines River. Official pages do not give a single shared calendar day for the 1900 reversal, and this card does not pick one. MWRD official news dated 20 October 2025 says the initial inflow into the Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal was on 2 January 1900. Illinois DNR official history says flow through the canal began on 17 January 1900. A later MWRD anniversary article dated 24 October 2025 says water officially flowed into the canal for the first time in January 1900, without a day. The American Society of Civil Engineers named the canal construction one of the 'Seven Wonders of American Engineering' in 1955, as stated on the same page.
